result.output:
1	# Session capability note
2	
3	Recorded while diagnosing why Entire reported zero checkpoints across the whole
4	build. The integration is installed and healthy; nothing was ever captured
5	because of when the plugin was installed, and that is worth writing down.
6	
7	## The symptom
8	
9	`entire status` reported enabled, `entire doctor` passed every check, the git
10	hooks fired on every commit, and `entire checkpoint list` still returned zero.
11	The dashboard read "Stalled. No activity." across all 55 commits.
12	
13	## What was actually true
14	
15	Three separate things each had to be true, and two of them looked true while
16	being false:
17	
18	1. **Hooks installed** — genuinely true. `pre-commit` ran `docs-check` on a
19	   normal commit, and `.entire/logs/entire.log` gained entries at each commit.
20	2. **Agent integration installed** — genuinely true. `entire agent list` showed
21	   `opencode` enabled, and `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` was committed hours
22	   before the commit under test.
23	3. **A session was registered** — false, and this is the one that mattered.
24	
25	The plugin fires `entire hooks opencode session-start` on the **`session.created`**
26	event. That event fires once, when a session opens. This repository's session
27	was already open when the plugin was installed, so it never fired, so Entire
28	never registered a session, so every commit had nothing to attach a checkpoint
29	to.
30	
31	`entire doctor` does not catch this: it verifies wiring, not registration. The
32	tell is that `.entire/` contains only `logs/` and `settings.json` — if session
33	state were being written, it would be there.
34	
35	## Why restarting did not obviously fix it
36	
37	Restarting OpenCode creates a new session, which *should* fire
38	`session.created`. But it is easy to conclude "I restarted, so it is working"
39	without a commit having been made in the new session, and a checkpoint only
40	appears once both have happened.
41	
42	## How to confirm, instead of assuming
43	
44	```bash
45	entire doctor                 # wiring only - can be green with zero sessions
46	entire checkpoint list       # the number that matters
47	tail -f .entire/logs/entire.log   # look for "session-start", not just "redaction configured"
48	```
49	
50	`"msg":"redaction configured"` on its own means hooks ran and found nothing to
51	attach to. `"msg":"session-start"` is the line that means capture is live.
52	
53	## Worth knowing for the demo
54	
55	Entire checkpoints record the **agent session** that produced a commit, not the
56	commit history. Git history is the durable record and is already complete; the
57	Entire graph is the extra evidence of how the code was written. This repo's
58	build predates session capture, so that evidence starts when capture starts —
59	it cannot be backfilled, because the session transcripts were never recorded.

Docs read. Here's Entire per [docs.entire.io](https://docs.entire.io/), grounded against this repo's actual state.

## What Entire is (from the docs)

- **Session storage** — every commit an agent makes becomes a *checkpoint*: the diff paired with the prompt, transcript, tool calls, and files behind it. Secrets are redacted before anything leaves the machine. ([Capture checkpoints](https://docs.entire.io/guides/checkpoints/capture-checkpoints.md))
- **Code hosting / mirrors** — distributed Git hosting so agents clone/pull from a nearby region; GitHub can stay source of truth via mirrors. (Not set up here.)
- **Agentic search** — one query over repos, commits, and sessions (`entire search`), plus `entire-graph` for symbol-level lookup.
- **How capture works** — two halves: agent hooks collect session context while you work; Git hooks link it to a commit with an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. A normal checkpoint needs **both** captured context **and** a commit. Setting `commit_linking: "always"` in `.entire/settings.json` skips the per-commit prompt.

## What's true in this repo right now

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| CLI installed | Yes — 0.11.4 |
| Enabled | Yes, branch `main`, agents: Claude Code + OpenCode |
| Session registered | **Yes** — `7f5ed5af`, this Claude Code session, active |
| `entire doctor` | All green (hooks, both agents, no stuck sessions) |
| Checkpoints on `main` | **0** |

## The important contrast with `docs/known-limits-entire.md`

That note records *why the whole build captured zero checkpoints*: hooks were installed but **no session was ever registered** (the OpenCode session predated the plugin install, so `session.created` never fired). `entire doctor` can't catch that — it verifies wiring, not registration.

This session is the opposite case: the Claude Code hooks fired `session-start` when this conversation opened, and `entire session current` resolves to my own session. So capture is live now — the next commit made from this session should produce this repo's first checkpoint (with the `[Y]es/[n]o/[a]lways` link prompt, unless `commit_linking` is set to `always`).

Want me to do anything with this — e.g. set `commit_linking: always`, update the known-limits note to record that capture is live, or leave things as-is?
